chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Playing behind the curtain in a swank Paris club
summary: Sarah is the only visible performer while the band led by a Martinique-born flautist plays behind the curtain, making cues a challenge.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But we were in Paris, and we opened at a very swanky club called the La Darpdor(?) -- I think the translation is The Golden Crepe. Anyway, it was just so high class. They had suits of armor around, and all kinds of drapes -- it looked like some room in a big castle somewhere. But we had a big band there that was very good. The guy who led the band was a flautist. He had played flute with bands over here. He was

originally from Martinique, I think, but he had lived in the United States and had played in bands over here, and he had a very good band over there. If I remember correctly, it must have been about at least 14 or 15 men.

The unique experience playing in Paris was that Sarah Vaughan went on stage, she was the only one on stage, I mean visible to the audience. The band played behind the curtain, including me. So, to actually communicate with her the way I had been proved a little problem to begin with, but we finally got cues together and things turned out all right. But it seems as if we were there at least three or four weeks, I believe.
